# Sheldon LuaVM – Full Documentation

> Scripting reference and API documentation for Sheldon's LuaVM, a customizable Lua scripting environment for Roblox.
> Source: https://www.projectsheldon.me/luavm/
> This plain-text file mirrors the full documentation for AI assistants and search tools.

---

## Sheldon's Scripting Environment

A Lua 5.4 environment that runs scripts inside the Sheldon overlay with direct access to the game, the renderer, input, files, networking and process memory.

### What runs

Scripts run in Lua 5.4, not Luau. The `base`, `math`, `table` and `string` libraries are available, and Lua 5.4's bitwise operators work without a `bit32` library.

Scripts also accept two Luau conveniences: type ascriptions (`local part: Part = ...` and `value :: Type`) and compound assignments (`+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `^=`, `..=`, `&=`, `|=`, `>=`). Type ascriptions are ignored at runtime but are used by [Auto Complete](#/autocomplete).

### Entry points

`game` is the DataModel. There is no separate `Game` or `workspace` global; use `game:GetService("Workspace")`, `game:GetService("Players")` and so on. Instances are wrapped by the [Instance](#/instance) type, which exposes their registered and reflected properties, children and methods.

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")
local me = Players.LocalPlayer

print(me.Name, me.DisplayName)
print(Workspace.Gravity)
```

`Players.LocalPlayer` and player character properties are read from the live process. See [Instance](#/instance) for property access rules and [RBXScriptSignal](#/signals) for events.

### Libraries

| Library | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| **globals** | `print`, `warn`, `typeof`, `loadstring`, `hex`, `tick` and the `math`/`string` additions |
| **task** | Coroutine scheduling and yields |
| **tween** | Property interpolation |
| **memory** | Typed process reads and writes |
| **cheat** | Frame events, custom ESP, game modules, GC access, raycasts, servers |
| **internet** | HTTP requests, including asynchronous POST |
| **input** | Mouse and keyboard simulation |
| **file** | Sandboxed file access |
| **draw** | 2D primitives on the overlay |
| **gui** | Runtime overlay tabs |
| **imgui** | Immediate-mode widgets and windows |
| **entity** | Custom entity registration for ESP and targeting |
| **fflags** | Client FastFlag reads and writes |
| **utility** | Clipboard access |
| **base64**, **hash**, **compress** | Encoding, hashing and LZ4 |

`memory`, `input`, `file`, `utility` and `internet` are gated. They throw a "library is not enabled" error until switched on in the Lua VM settings. See [Library Gating](#/library-gating).

### Editor

The script editor keeps multiple tabs, runs each tab independently, and exposes Execute, Stop, Restart, Save and Upload. Files can be marked Auto Execute per place or for the current session. The console below the editor receives `print`, `warn` and runtime errors.

[Auto Complete](#/autocomplete) reads the current game and the Lua environment, so it lists instance children, writable and read-only properties, library functions, services, FFlags, key names and type names as you type.

### Minimal script

```lua
cheat.Register("onPaint", function()
    local root = game:GetService("Players").LocalPlayer.Character
    if not root then return end

    local pos, onScreen = cheat.WorldToScreen(root.HumanoidRootPart.Position)
    if onScreen then
        draw.TextOutlined("you", pos.x, pos.y, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
    end
end)
```

## Auto Complete

The editor completes against the current game and the Lua environment, not a fixed list of names.

Completion is part of the script editor. It offers the members of the value before a `.` or `:`. The list includes instance properties that are not written into this documentation, so it stays current with the game.

### Opening and accepting

| Action | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Type an identifier | Suggestions open immediately while you type |
| `Ctrl` + `Space` | Opens the full suggestion list, including locals |
| `Tab` or `Enter` | Accepts the highlighted row |
| `Tab` a second time | For a method, appends `()`; for a writable property, appends `= ` |
| `Tab` during a snippet | Jumps to the next `$` stop |
| `Esc` | Closes the popup |

### What is completed

| Context | Suggestions |
| --- | --- |
| Anywhere | Local variables declared so far, functions, globals, library names, known type names |
| `value.` / `value:` | Table keys, userdata members, instance children, methods and properties |
| `game:GetService("...")` | Services and other children of the DataModel |
| `instance:FindFirstChild("...")`, `WaitForChild` | Child names of that instance |
| `instance:FindFirstChildOfClass("...")`, `FindDescendantsOfClass` | Class names |
| `instance:FindDescendants("...")` | Descendant names of that instance |
| `instance:IsA("...")` | Known class names and `Instance` |
| `instance:GetAttribute("...")`, `SetAttribute` | Attribute names on that instance, with their types |
| `instance:HasTag("...")`, `AddTag`, `RemoveTag`, `GetTag`, `RenameTag` | Tags on that instance |
| `instance:GetPropertyChangedSignal("...")` | Registered and reflected property names for that class |
| `:: ` | Class names, usertypes and primitive type names |
| `fflags.Get("...")`, `fflags.Set("...")` | FFlag names from the client, plus read/write memory types in the type argument |
| `memory.Read(address, "...")`, `memory.Write(address, value, "...")` | Readable or writable memory types |
| `input.IsHeld("...")` and the other key functions | Windows key names for the current layout |
| `draw.Text(..., "...")`, `TextOutlined`, `GetTextSize` | Loaded font names |
| `gui.AddTab("...")`, `RemoveTab`, `IsTab` | Existing tab names |
| `entity.AddEntity("...")` and the other entity functions | Registered entity keys |
| `cheat.Register("...")`, `Unregister` | Event names |
| `cheat.SetEspOrder("...")`, `UnregisterEsp` | Registered ESP ids |
| `cheat.TeleportPlace("...")`, `GetServers` | Job ids from the last server list |
| `tween.Info(time, delay, "...")` | Easing style names |
| `file.write("...")` and the other file functions | Files and folders in the sandbox |

Instance rows show child names with their class icon, functions with a function icon, writable properties with a property icon, and read-only properties with a separate icon. Gated libraries that are switched off appear as `name [Disabled]` and are inserted without being callable.

### Type hints

Type ascriptions are ignored at runtime, but completion uses them when the value is not available yet:

```lua
local part: Part = game:GetService("Workspace").SomePart
part. -- Position, Size, Transparency, Anchored, ...

local character: Model = player.Character
character:FindFirstChild(" -- child names

local value = game:GetService("Workspace").SomePart :: Part
value:GetPropertyChangedSignal(" -- property names for Part
```

Ascriptions also work on loop variables when the iterator is a known instance call:

```lua
for _, child in ipairs(game:GetService("Workspace"):GetChildren()) do
    child. -- child is completed as an Instance
end
```

Locals assigned from known game values are inferred without an ascription, for example `local players = game:GetService("Players")`.

### Snippets

Typing one of these names offers a snippet. Tab moves through the numbered stops.

| Trigger | Expands to |
| --- | --- |
| `if` | `if ... then ... end` |
| `while` | `while ... do ... end` |
| `fordo` | Numeric `for` loop |
| `forpairs` | `for k, v in pairs(...) do` |
| `foripairs` | `for i, v in ipairs(...) do` |
| `repeat` | `repeat ... until ...` |
| `func` | Global function |
| `localfunc` | Local function |
| `local` | `local name = value` |
| `return` | `return value` |
| `pcall` | `local ok, err = pcall(function() ... end)` |

### Settings

The editor exposes two completion switches in the autocomplete settings:

- **Find first child completion** – enables the string-argument lists such as `FindFirstChild("`, `GetAttribute("`, `GetService("`, FFlag names, key names and file names.

- **Find first child auto trigger** – opens that list automatically when you type the opening quote inside one of those calls. With it off, press `Ctrl` + `Space` inside the string.

### Relationship to Class Properties

The old **Class Properties** page listed a hand-picked subset of properties. That list went stale whenever a class gained a property, and it could not show children of the current game. This page replaces it: completion uses the current game, so it lists every property the game exposes and shows which ones are writable.

---

## Global Functions

Built-in global functions available in the LuaVM environment.

| Function | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **print(...)** | Writes to the console with a `[print]` prefix |
| **warn(...)** | Writes to the console with a `[warn]` prefix |
| **error(...)** | Raises a Lua error with the formatted arguments |
| **typeof(v)** | Like `type`, but returns `"Instance"` for wrapped Roblox instances instead of `"userdata"` |
| **type(v)** | Lua's `type`, extended for addresses returned by `cheat.getgc`. Those return `"string"`, `"table"`, `"function"`, `"userdata"` or `"thread"`. All other values behave normally. |
| **hex(number)** | Formats an integer as an uppercase hex string, e.g. `0x7FF6A2C1` |
| **tick()** | Returns milliseconds since the system started, not a UNIX timestamp |
| **loadstring(source)** | Compiles source after stripping Luau type ascriptions. Returns `(function, nil)` or `(nil, error_message)` |
| **getfenv([f])** | Returns the global table. The argument is accepted for compatibility but does not change the result |
| **setfenv(f, env)** | No-op, kept for scripts that probe for it |

### Math Additions

Appended to Lua's `math` library:

| Function | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **math.ldexp(x, exp)** | `number` | Returns `x * 2^exp` |
| **math.frexp(x)** | `number, number` | Splits `x` into mantissa and exponent |
| **math.round(x)** | `number` | Rounds to the nearest integer, halfway away from zero |

### String Extensions

Appended to Lua's built-in `string` library:

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **string.regex(text, pattern)** | `string, string` | Returns `true` when the pattern matches. It uses ECMAScript regular expressions, not Lua patterns. Invalid patterns return `false`. |

#### Example

```lua
-- ECMAScript syntax: \d+, not Lua's %d+
if string.regex("hello123", "\\d+") then
    print("contains digits")
end

-- type() also reports the type of addresses returned by getgc
local gc = cheat.getgc()
for _, t in next, gc do
    if type(t) == "table" then
        -- t is an address, but type() reports "table".
    end
end
```

---

## base64

Base64 encoding and decoding. Always available (no library gate).

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **base64.Encode(data)** | `string` | Encodes a string to base64. Input is limited to 10 MB. |
| **base64.Decode(data)** | `string` | Decodes a base64 string. Invalid input raises an error; output is limited to 10 MB. |

### Example

```lua
local encoded = base64.Encode("Hello, world!")
print(encoded)  -- SGVsbG8sIHdvcmxkIQ==
local decoded = base64.Decode(encoded)
print(decoded)  -- Hello, world!
```

---

## hash

Cryptographic hash functions. Always available (no library gate).

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **hash.Sha256(data)** | `string` | Returns a lowercase SHA-256 hex digest. Input is limited to 10 MB. |
| **hash.Sha3(data)** | `string` | Returns a lowercase SHA3-256 hex digest. Input is limited to 10 MB. |
| **hash.Md5(data)** | `string` | Returns a lowercase MD5 hex digest. Input is limited to 10 MB. |

### Example

```lua
local sha = hash.Sha256("hello")
print(sha)  -- 2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824
```

---

## compress

LZ4 compression. Always available (no library gate).

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **compress.Compress(data)** | `string` | Compresses a string with LZ4 and returns the raw compressed bytes. Input is limited to 10 MB. The original size is not stored. |
| **compress.Decompress(data)** | `string` | Expects a 4-byte little-endian original size followed by LZ4 data, and returns the decompressed string. |

**Current mismatch:** `compress.Compress` does not write the size header that `compress.Decompress` reads. Round-tripping through these two functions does not work yet. Store the original length separately if you need to decompress data outside the VM.

### Example

```lua
local comp = compress.Compress("Hello, world!")
print(#comp)  -- raw LZ4 bytes, no size header
```

---

## task

Scheduling utilities for asynchronous execution.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **task.spawn(fn, ...)** | `function, ...` | Runs `fn` asynchronously. Extra arguments are passed to `fn`. |
| **task.defer(fn, ...)** | `function, ...` | Runs `fn` asynchronously, like `task.spawn`. |
| **task.delay(seconds, fn)** | `number, function` | Runs `fn` after `seconds`. |
| **task.wait(seconds?)** | `number?` | Yields the current coroutine and returns the measured elapsed time. Defaults to `0`. Calling it from the main script body raises an error; wrap the script in `task.spawn` first. |

### Example

```lua
task.spawn(function()
    print("Runs asynchronously!")
end)

task.defer(function(a, b)
    print("deferred", a, b)
end, "with", "arguments")

task.delay(2, function()
    print("two seconds later")
end)

task.spawn(function()
    local elapsed = task.wait(1)
    print("Waited", elapsed, "seconds")
end)
```

---

## tween

Interpolate instance properties smoothly over time. Modelled on Roblox's TweenService.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **tween.Info(time, delayTime?, style?)** | `number, number?, string\|int?` | Builds a TweenInfo table. `style` defaults to `"Linear"`, `delayTime` to `0`. You can also pass a raw table `{time=..., delayTime=..., style=...}` anywhere info is expected. |
| **tween.Create(instance, info, props)** | `Instance, table, table` | Creates a tween that interpolates each property in `props` from its current value to the target value. Returns a tween object. The target must still be alive when the tween plays. |

### Tween Object

| Method | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **tween:Play(waitForFinish?)** | `bool?` | Starts the tween. When `waitForFinish` is `true`, blocks the calling coroutine until every property has finished tweening; otherwise returns immediately. Both `tween:Play(...)` and `tween.Play(...)` syntaxes are accepted. |
| **tween:Cancel()** |  | Snaps every property back to the value it had when the tween was created. The tween itself keeps running, so values may move again; let it finish or overwrite the property to stop it. |

### Easing Styles

`Linear`, `Bounce`, `Elastic`, `Exponential`, `Cubic`. Also exposed as `tween.EasingStyle.Linear` etc. for readability. Pass either the string, the constant, or an integer index (`0` = Linear through `4` = Cubic). Unknown styles fall back to `Linear`.

### Supported Property Types

- `number` – e.g. `Transparency`, `Reflectance`, `WalkSpeed`

- `Vector3` – e.g. `Position`, `Size`, `LinearVelocity`, `AngularVelocity`

- `Color3` – e.g. `Color`

Common classes such as `Part`, `MeshPart` and `VehicleSeat` are supported directly. Other classes work as long as the game exposes the property.

The property must be writable on that instance. [Auto Complete](#/autocomplete) lists what is available for the selected instance. Read-only properties, unknown names and unsupported value types raise an error at `tween.Create` time.

### Example – Move a part

```lua
local part = game:GetService("Workspace").Part
local info = tween.Info(1.5, 0, "Cubic")

local t = tween.Create(part, info, {
    Position = Vector3.new(0, 20, 0),
    Transparency = 0.5,
})

t:Play()
```

### Example – Wait until finished

```lua
local part = game:GetService("Workspace").Part

local t = tween.Create(part, { time = 2, style = "Bounce" }, {
    Position = part.Position + Vector3.new(0, 15, 0),
})

t:Play(true)
print("Tween finished – running follow-up code")
```

### Example – Chained tweens

```lua
task.spawn(function()
    local part = game:GetService("Workspace").Part
    local up   = tween.Create(part, tween.Info(1, 0, "Cubic"),  { Position = part.Position + Vector3.new(0, 10, 0) })
    local down = tween.Create(part, tween.Info(1, 0, "Bounce"), { Position = part.Position })

    up:Play()
    task.wait(1)
    down:Play()
    task.wait(1)
end)
```

### Notes

- Each property tweens independently. Passing multiple properties runs them in parallel on the same schedule.

- `tween:Play(true)` waits until every property finishes and pauses all scripts while waiting. `task.spawn` does not avoid this. Use `Play()` without the flag and schedule follow-up work with `task.delay`.

- Physics-driven properties (`Position`, `CFrame`, velocities) update visually, but the engine may resimulate them on the next physics step; combine with anchoring or velocity-zeroing for full control.

- Tweens continue while the script is yielded.

---

## memory

Raw memory read/write operations. Requires the Memory library to be enabled.

Requires: Memory library enabled

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **memory.Read(address, type)** | `uintptr, string` | Reads from memory and converts to the given type. Unknown or write-only types raise an error. |
| **memory.Write(address, value)** | `uintptr, any` | Writes a value, choosing the width from its Lua type |
| **memory.Write(address, value, type)** | `uintptr, any, string` | Writes a value using an explicit type |
| **memory.GetRTTI(address)** | `uintptr` | Returns the class name for an object address, or `???` when the address cannot be read. |
| **memory.GetBase()** |  | Returns the Roblox process base address |
| **memory.Rebase(offset)** | `uintptr` | Returns `base + offset` |

### Supported Types

**Read/Write:** `float`, `double`, `int`, `uint`, `bool`, `byte`, `short`, `ushort`, `int64`, `uint64`, `string`, `vector2`, `vector3`, `color3`.

**Write also supports:** `pointer`.

Vectors accept a `Vector2`/`Vector3`/`Color3` value or a table (`{x, y, z}`, `{r, g, b}`, or `{1, 2, 3}`).

### Write Auto-Decision

When the `type` argument is omitted, `memory.Write` decides the width from the value:

| Value | Written as |
| --- | --- |
| `integer` in int32 range (e.g. `999`) | `int32` (4 bytes) |
| `integer` outside int32 range | `int64` (8 bytes) |
| `float` (e.g. `0.123`) | `float` (4 bytes) |
| `boolean` | `bool` |
| `string` (e.g. `"abc123"`) | null-terminated string |
| `Vector2` or `{x, y}` | 2 floats (8 bytes) |
| `Vector3` / `Color3` or `{x, y, z}` | 3 floats (12 bytes) |

Pass `type` explicitly when the field needs a different width (e.g. a `double` field, a `byte` flag, or a pointer).

### Example

```lua
local base = memory.GetBase()
local hp = memory.Read(base + 0x1234, "float")
print(hex(hp))
memory.Write(base + 0x1234, 999, "int")
memory.Write(base + 0x1238, 0.123)
memory.Write(base + 0x1238, 0.123, "double")
memory.Write(base + 0x1240, "abc123", "string")
memory.Write(base + 0x1250, Vector3.new(1, 2, 3), "vector3")
```

---

## cheat

Frame events, custom ESP elements, game modules, raycasting, server and teleport helpers, and direct access to the Roblox Luau garbage collector.

### Events

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Register(eventType, fn)** | `string, function` | Register a callback for an event type. Fires for the lifetime of the script until unregistered. |
| **Unregister(eventType, fn)** | `string, function` | Unregister a previously registered callback. Pass the same function reference used with `Register`. |

#### Event Types

| Event | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **onPaint** | Runs every rendered frame. Drawing belongs here. |
| **onUpdate** | Runs frequently, on the game's update |
| **onSlowUpdate** | Runs less often than `onUpdate` |
| **teleport** | Runs when the player teleports |

Callbacks receive no arguments and cannot yield. Errors are written to the console and the callback stays registered. `Register` raises `unknown cheat event` for a bad name; `Unregister` silently returns for unknown names or functions that were never registered.

#### Example

```lua
local function onPaint()
    draw.Text("ESP Label", 100, 50, Color3.new(1, 1, 0))
end

cheat.Register("onPaint", onPaint)

-- Later, stop drawing:
cheat.Unregister("onPaint", onPaint)
```

### Custom ESP

Adds an element to the ESP layout. It uses the same anchors, ordering and drag behaviour as the built-in labels, and is removed when the script stops or the id is unregistered.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **RegisterEsp(id, options)** | `string, table` | Registers or replaces an ESP element. The id must be non-empty and must not collide with a built-in element or a reserved name. |
| **SetEspOrder(id, order)** | `string, number` | Changes the element's sort order. Lower numbers render first. Default is `15`. |
| **UnregisterEsp(id)** | `string` | Removes the element. |

#### Options

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `function` | Called per player with the player table. Returns the label text and optionally a `Color3`. |
| `measure` | `function` | Called per player with the player table. Must return `width, height` numbers, used when the element is positioned or dragged. |
| `draw` | `function` | Called per player as `draw(player, x, y, w, h)` after layout. Use the draw library inside it. |
| `anchor` | `string` | `Top` (default), `Bottom`, `TopLeft`, `TopRight`, `BottomLeft`, `BottomRight`, `CenterLeft`, `CenterRight` |
| `order` | `number` | Sort order, default `15` |
| `enabled` | `bool` | Whether the element is drawn, default `true` |
| `color` | `Color3` or table | Default text color, default white. Tables use `r, g, b` or `1, 2, 3` and accept 0-1 or 0-255 values. |

At least one of `text`, `measure` or `draw` is required. A Lua error inside a callback disables that ESP with an error in the console instead of retrying every frame.

#### Player table

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | `number` | Player instance address |
| `username` | `string` | Account name |
| `displayName` | `string` | Display name |
| `userId` | `number` | User id |
| `health`, `maxHealth` | `number` | Current and maximum health |
| `team` | `string` | Team name |
| `isSameTeam` | `bool` | Whether the player shares the local team |
| `isAlive` | `bool` | Alive state |
| `isActiveUser` | `bool` | Whether the player is marked as an active user |
| `position` | `Vector3` | Head position |
| `distance` | `number` | Distance from the local head to this player's head |

#### Example

```lua
cheat.RegisterEsp("Distance", {
    anchor = "Top",
    order = 4,
    color = Color3.new(1, 1, 1),
    text = function(player)
        return string.format("%s [%dm]", player.username, math.floor(player.distance))
    end,
    measure = function(player)
        return 120, 14
    end,
    draw = function(player, x, y, w, h)
        draw.Rect(x - 2, y - 1, w + 4, h + 2, Color3.new(0, 0, 0), 1, 2, 0.6)
    end,
})
```

### Custom game module

Some games parent characters outside `Players` or use a bone layout the default module cannot read. `RegisterGame` installs a Lua replacement for the module that finds player roots, reads player data and returns bones. Only one Lua game module can be active; registering another replaces it.

**Manual run only:** `RegisterGame` refuses to run from auto-execute or session auto-load, and it also refuses when the current place id is not in `placeIds`. Execute it from the editor.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **RegisterGame(definition)** | `table` | Registers the module, adds a tab named after `name`, and makes it the active game module. |
| **UnregisterGame()** |  | Removes the module if the calling script owns it. The default module returns. |

#### Definition

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Required. Tab name and module name. |
| `placeIds` | `table` | Required. Place ids this module accepts. Numbers or numeric strings. |
| `getParents` | `function` | Optional. Returns a table of Instances that contain the player models. Returning nothing falls back to `Players`. |
| `getPlayer` | `function` | Optional. Called with a parent Instance; returns a table with `Character`/`model`, `userId`, `username`/`Name`, `displayName`/`DisplayName`, `Team`/`teamName`, `Humanoid`, `rigType` and `bones`. |
| `getBones` | `function` | Optional. Called as `getBones(character, rigType)`; returns a table of bone name to Instance. Names such as `Head`, `HumanoidRootPart`, `UpperTorso`, `LeftUpperArm` and `RightFoot` are read. |
| `onUpdate` | `function` | Optional. Runs once per module update. Errors are reported to the console. |

#### Example

```lua
cheat.RegisterGame({
    name = "My Game",
    placeIds = { 123456789 },
    getParents = function()
        return { game:GetService("Workspace").Characters }
    end,
    getPlayer = function(parent)
        local model = parent:FindFirstChild("Dummy")
        if not model then return nil end
        return {
            Character = model,
            Humanoid = model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid"),
            username = model.Name,
            displayName = model.Name,
            teamName = "Neutral",
        }
    end,
})
```

### Garbage Collector

Read and write values in the game's Lua objects. `getgc` lists objects or finds a key; `rawget` and `rawset` work on one object address; `setgc` writes a key.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **getgc(includeAll?)** | `bool?` | Returns an array of GC object addresses. The default returns tables only; `true` also includes strings, functions, userdata and threads. Use `type(address)` to identify each entry. |
| **getgc(key)** | `string` | Returns the value of the first object that has `key`. Object values come back as addresses. Returns `nil` when nothing matches. Cannot be combined with the boolean form. |
| **setgc(key, value)** | `string, bool \| number \| address` | Writes to the first object that has `key`. Accepts `bool`, `number`, or an address for object values. Strings must be passed as an existing string address. Missing keys are ignored. |
| **rawget(addr, key \| true)** | `number, string \| bool` | Reads a field from the object at `addr`. Pass a `string` key for one field, or `true` to dump the whole table. Missing keys return `nil`. Object values come back as addresses. |
| **rawset(addr, key, value)** | `number, string, any` | Writes an existing field on the object at `addr`. Accepts `nil`, `bool`, `number`, or an address for object values. Returns `true` on success and `false` if the key does not exist. |

#### Example

```lua
-- Walk every table once. This is the only form that visits all of them.
for _, t in next, cheat.getgc() do
    if type(t) == "table"
       and cheat.rawget(t, "MaxAmmo") ~= nil then
        cheat.rawset(t, "MaxAmmo",     math.huge)
        cheat.rawset(t, "CurrentAmmo", math.huge)
    end
end

-- Key lookup returns the first match only, not every table.
local ammo = cheat.getgc("MaxAmmo")
if ammo then print("first MaxAmmo seen =", ammo) end

-- setgc also writes the first table that has the key.
cheat.setgc("MaxAmmo",     math.huge)
cheat.setgc("CurrentAmmo", math.huge)

-- Dump every field on a table (debugging).
local dump = cheat.rawget(someAddr, true)
for k, v in pairs(dump) do print(k, "=", v) end
```

### Raycast

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Raycast(pos, dir, distance?, ignoreTransparent?)** | `Vector3, Vector3, number?, bool?` | Casts a ray through the cached world scene. `distance` defaults to `1000`; intersections closer than 4 studs are ignored. `ignoreTransparent` skips invisible parts. Returns `(missed, instance, position, distance)`: the first value is `true` when nothing was hit, `instance` is then invalid and `position` is `(0, 0, 0)`. On a hit, `distance` is the hit distance; on a miss it is the maximum. |

The scene comes from the cached Workspace parts, not from Roblox's own raycast API, so very new parts can lag by one cache refresh and parts outside the streamed region are not present.

#### Example

```lua
local missed, inst, pos, dist = cheat.Raycast(
    Vector3.new(0, 5, 0),
    Vector3.new(0, -1, 0),
    500
)

if not missed then
    print("hit", inst.Name, "at", pos, "dist", dist)
end
```

### World To Screen

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **WorldToScreen(worldPos)** | `Vector3` | Project world position to screen. Returns `(Vector2 screenPos, bool isOnScreen)`. |

#### Example

```lua
-- Project a player's position to screen
local character = player.Character
if not character then return end

local screen, onScreen = cheat.WorldToScreen(character.HumanoidRootPart.Position)
if onScreen then
    draw.Text("Player", screen.x, screen.y, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
end
```

### Servers & Teleport

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **TeleportPlace(placeId, jobId?)** | `string, string?` | Teleport to a Roblox place/server. Also accepts a table `{PlaceId, JobId}`. Returns `bool`. |
| **GetServers(placeId?)** | `string?` | Fetches game server list. Returns table of servers with `JobId, PlaceId, UniverseId, GameName, Playing, MaxPlayers, Ping, Fps`. Defaults to current place. |
| **GetUniverseId(placeId?)** | `string?` | Gets universe ID for a place. Defaults to current place. |

#### Example

```lua
-- Teleport to a place
local ok = cheat.TeleportPlace("123456789")
print("Teleport:", ok)

-- Get servers for current place
local servers = cheat.GetServers()
for _, srv in ipairs(servers) do
    print(srv.JobId, srv.Playing, "/", srv.MaxPlayers)
end
```

### Payload Execution

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **RunSecure(payload)** | `string` | Runs an obfuscated payload produced by the Obfuscate page. Paste the generated snippet as-is – it already wraps the payload in this call. |

#### Example

```lua
-- Output from the Obfuscate page: run it like any other script.
local kQ8d2fA=19584732;
cheat.RunSecure("U09CMQ...")
```

## internet

HTTP GET and POST with request headers, timeouts and an asynchronous POST path for the render thread. Requires the Internet library to be enabled.

Requires: Internet library enabled

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **internet.get(url, timeout?, info?)** | `string, number?, table?` | Blocking GET. Returns `{ text = string, status_code = number }`. |
| **internet.post(url, body?, timeout?, info?)** | `string, string?, number?, table?` | Blocking POST. Returns the same table. The body defaults to an empty string. |
| **internet.postasync(url, body?, timeout?, info?, callback?)** | `string, string?, number?, table?, function?` | Runs the POST on a worker thread. Without a callback it yields and returns `result` or `nil, error`. With a callback it returns nothing and calls `callback(result, error)` on the VM worker. |

### Arguments

| Argument | Details |
| --- | --- |
| `url` | Must start with `https://`. The Require HTTPS setting can be turned off in the Lua VM settings, which also allows `http://`. Maximum 2048 characters. |
| `timeout` | Milliseconds, default `5000`, clamped to `1-15000`. `0` is raised to `1`. |
| `body` | String, maximum 10 MB. |
| `info` | Table with a `headers` sub-table. Header names must be non-empty and at most 1024 characters; values at most 8192. CR, LF and NUL are rejected. A browser User-Agent is added when missing. |
| Response | Responses larger than 10 MB raise `response too big >10mb`. Network failures raise a Lua error; the callback form receives the error message instead. |

### Render thread

`internet.get` and `internet.post` refuse to run inside a `gui.AddTab` callback because they would freeze the overlay. Use `postasync` with a callback there, or push the work into `task.spawn` and call a blocking function from the worker.

### Examples

```lua
local res = internet.get("https://api.example.com/data", 5000)
print(res.status_code)
print(res.text)

local posted = internet.post(
    "https://api.example.com/items",
    '{"name":"item"}',
    5000,
    { headers = { ["Content-Type"] = "application/json" } }
)
```

Callback form, safe on the render thread:

```lua
internet.postasync("https://api.example.com/items", "{}", 5000, nil, function(result, err)
    if err then
        warn("request failed:", err)
        return
    end

    print(result.status_code, result.text)
end)
```

Yield form, inside a coroutine:

```lua
task.spawn(function()
    local result, err = internet.postasync("https://api.example.com/items", "{}")
    if err then
        warn("request failed:", err)
        return
    end

    print(result.status_code, result.text)
end)
```

---

## input

Mouse and keyboard input simulation. Requires the Input library to be enabled.

Requires: Input library enabled

### Mouse

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **input.MoveMouse(dir, relative?)** | `Vector2, bool?` | Moves the mouse to an absolute overlay position, or by a delta when `relative` is true. The resulting position must stay strictly inside the overlay, otherwise it raises an error. |
| **input.GetMousePosition()** |  | Returns the current cursor position as a `Vector2` |
| **input.MouseClick(click, time?)** | `int, int?` | Clicks a button (1 = left, 2 = right). `time` is the hold time in ms, default `50` |
| **input.MousePress(click)** | `int` | Presses a button and leaves it down |
| **input.MouseRelease(click)** | `int` | Releases a button |
| **input.GetScrollDelta()** |  | Returns the current scroll-wheel delta |
| **input.GetMoveDelta()** |  | Returns the frame's mouse movement as a `Vector2` |

### Keyboard

Keys can be Windows virtual-key codes or the display names returned by `GetKeyNameTextA` for the current layout, matched case-insensitively. Autocomplete lists the names. Examples: `"W"`, `"Space"`, `"Left Shift"`, `"Up"`, `"F1"`.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **input.IsHeld(vKey)** | `int\|string` | True while the key is down |
| **input.IsPressed(vKey)** | `int\|string` | True on the frame the key went down |
| **input.IsReleased(vKey)** | `int\|string` | True on the frame the key went up |
| **input.PressKey(vKey, time?)** | `int\|string, int?` | Presses and releases a key. `time` is the hold time in ms, default `0` |
| **input.HoldKey(vKey)** | `int\|string` | Holds a key down |
| **input.ReleaseKey(vKey)** | `int\|string` | Releases a key |
| **input.Type(text, time?)** | `string, int?` | Types text character by character with an optional delay between characters |

### Example

```lua
-- Center mouse and click
input.MoveMouse(Vector2.new(960, 540))
input.MouseClick(1)

-- Type a message
input.Type("Hello, world!", 50)
```

## file

Sandboxed file system operations. Requires the File_Management library to be enabled.

Requires: File_Management library enabled

All operations are sandboxed to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Penguu\Sheldon\scripts\SandboxEnv\`. Absolute paths, drive names and `..` components are rejected. `write` and `rename` create parent folders as needed.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **file.write(location, content)** | `string, string` | Writes or truncates a file. Content is limited to 10 MB. |
| **file.read(location)** | `string` | Reads a file as binary text. Files over 10 MB raise an error. |
| **file.rename(location, newName)** | `string, string` | Moves or renames a file inside the sandbox. Both paths are resolved inside the sandbox. |
| **file.delete(location)** | `string` | Deletes a file. Missing paths raise an error. |
| **file.list(location)** | `string` | Returns an array of entry names. Stops after 256 entries and does not recurse. |
| **file.append(location, content)** | `string, string` | Appends to a file, creating it if needed. The resulting file is capped at 10 MB. |

The path argument autocompletes from the sandbox directory.

### Example

```lua
file.write("config.txt", "Hello, world!")
local content = file.read("config.txt")
print(content)
file.delete("config.txt")
```

---

## utility

System clipboard access. Requires the Clipboard library to be enabled.

Requires: Clipboard library enabled

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **utility.GetClipboard()** |  | Returns clipboard text, or an empty string when the clipboard is locked or holds no ANSI text |
| **utility.SetClipboard(text)** | `string` | Replaces the clipboard with ANSI text |

### Example

```lua
utility.SetClipboard("hello")
local text = utility.GetClipboard()
print(text)
```

Both functions raise `Clipboard library is not enabled` when the gate is off. They use the Win32 clipboard directly, so they only see `CF_TEXT` content; images and Unicode-only formats are not returned.

## entity

Adds non-player models to the same cache the built-in ESP, targeting and combat modules read.

An entity is a regular character model with a fake negative user id. Once added, it behaves like a player for ESP, aimbot and other modules that read the player cache. The local character cannot be added.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **entity.AddEntity(key, data)** | `string, table` | Adds an entity under `key`. Returns `true` on success, or `false` when the model is the local character. `Character`, `PrimaryPart` and `Name` are required. |
| **entity.EditEntity(key, data)** | `string, table` | Updates any of the same fields. Missing fields are left unchanged. Returns `false` for an unknown key. |
| **entity.RemoveEntity(key)** | `string` | Removes the entity and stops its update thread. Returns `false` if the key is unknown. |
| **entity.Clear()** |  | Removes every entity, not real players. Returns `true`. |
| **entity.GetEntity(key)** | `string` | Returns the entity table or `nil`. Fields: `Character`, `PrimaryPart`, `Name`, `DisplayName`, `Team`, `Humanoid`, `MaxHealth`, `Health`, `UserId`, `IsEntity`. |
| **entity.GetPlayers(includeEnemies?, includeEntities?)** | `bool?, bool?` | Returns an array of player and entity tables. Defaults: `includeEnemies = true`, `includeEntities = false`. |
| **entity.GetPositions(opts?)** | `table?` | Returns the cached positions of every player, the same data the built-in ESP draws from. It reads no game memory, so it is safe and fast to call every frame inside `onPaint`. See Positions table below. |

### Positions table

`entity.GetPositions` is the recommended way to follow players in `onPaint`. The cache is updated every frame by Sheldon, so drawings stay as smooth as the built-in ESP. A `task.spawn` loop that reads `Position` itself only updates a few times per second and looks choppy.

| Option | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `IncludeLocal` | `false` | Include the local player. |
| `IncludeEntities` | `false` | Include entities added with `AddEntity`. |
| `Bones` | `false` | Add a `Bones` table to each entry. Only enable it for skeletons or per-part boxes, as it creates many tables every frame. |

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Name` / `DisplayName` | `string` | Username and display name. |
| `UserId` | `number` | User id (negative for entities). |
| `IsLocal`, `IsEntity`, `IsEnemy`, `IsFriend` | `bool` | Flags from the player cache. |
| `Health` / `MaxHealth` | `number` | Cached health. `MaxHealth` is at least 1. |
| `RigType` | `string` | `"R6"` or `"R15"`. |
| `Distance` | `number` | Studs from the camera to the root. |
| `Position` | `Vector3` | Root part position. |
| `Head` | `Vector3` | Head position. |
| `Top` / `Bottom` | `Vector3` | Points above the head and below the feet, computed like the built-in ESP box. |
| `Center` | `Vector3` | Torso center. |
| `Bones` | `table` | Only with `Bones = true`. Map of part name (`"Head"`, `"HumanoidRootPart"`, R15 `"UpperTorso"`, `"LeftUpperArm"`, ..., R6 `"Torso"`, `"Left Arm"`, ...) to `{ Position, Size, RightVector, UpVector, LookVector }`, all `Vector3`. |

A bone's corners are `Position ± RightVector * Size.x / 2 ± UpVector * Size.y / 2 ± LookVector * Size.z / 2`.

```lua
cheat.Register("onPaint", function()
    for _, e in ipairs(entity.GetPositions()) do
        local top, topVisible = cheat.WorldToScreen(e.Top)
        local bottom, bottomVisible = cheat.WorldToScreen(e.Bottom)
        if topVisible and bottomVisible then
            local h = bottom.y - top.y
            local w = h * 0.5
            draw.Rect(top.x - w / 2, top.y, w, h, Color3.new(1, 0.3, 0.3), 1, 2, 1)
            draw.TextOutlined(e.Name, top.x - w / 2, top.y - 16, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
        end
    end
end)
```

### Entity fields

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Character` | `Instance` | Required. Model to treat as the character. |
| `PrimaryPart` | `Instance` | Required. Used as the root part for distance, targeting and ESP. |
| `Name` | `string` | Required. Shown in ESP and used as the username. |
| `DisplayName` | `string` | Optional display name, defaults to `Name`. |
| `Team` | `Team` or `string` | A Team instance, or a team name. A name without a color gets a default color. |
| `TeamColor` | `Color3` | Used with a string `Team` to build the team's BrickColor. |
| `DoTeamCheck` | `bool` | When true, compares the entity's team with the local team for `IsEnemy`. |
| `Humanoid` | `Instance` | Optional Humanoid. Found on the character when omitted. |
| `MaxHealth` / `Health` | `number` or `function` | A fixed value, or a zero-argument function evaluated whenever health is read. Defaults to the Humanoid values. |
| `RemoveOnDeath` | `bool` | Removes the entity when the Humanoid dies. Default `false`. |
| `Bones` | `table` | Optional map of bone name to Instance. Without it, bones are discovered from the character's children using its rig type. |

### Player table

`GetPlayers` returns every field from `GetEntity` plus `IsAlive`, `IsCameraVisible`, `IsLocal`, `IsPreview`, `IsTargeted`, `IsFriend`, `IsWhitelisted`, `IsEnemy` and `RigType` (`"R6"` or `"R15"`).

### Example

```lua
entity.AddEntity("target", {
    Character = char,
    PrimaryPart = char.HumanoidRootPart,
    Name = "Player1",
    Team = "Enemies",
    TeamColor = Color3.new(1, 0.3, 0.3),
    Health = function()
        return char.Humanoid.Health
    end,
})

local data = entity.GetEntity("target")
if data then
    print(data.Name, data.Health, data.PrimaryPart.Position)
end

for _, player in ipairs(entity.GetPlayers(true, true)) do
    print(player.Name, player.RigType, player.IsEntity)
end
```

---

## draw

Immediate 2D primitives drawn on the overlay's background draw list.

All functions draw immediately. Call them from `cheat.Register("onPaint", ...)`, an ESP `draw` callback, or a `gui.AddTab` callback. Coordinates are pixels in the overlay window. Colors are `Color3` with 0-1 components unless noted; `alpha` is 0-1.

Drawing functions only work on the overlay's render thread. Calling them from the script body, a `task.spawn` loop or a signal handler raises an error. `draw.ComputeConvexHull` and `draw.GetPartCorners` are pure helpers and work anywhere.

### Keeping it smooth

`onPaint` runs every frame. Keep it to math and drawing:

- For players, call `entity.GetPositions()` inside `onPaint`. It reads Sheldon's cache, not the game.

- For anything else (parts, tools, map objects), read the game in one `task.spawn` loop with `task.wait(0.03)` or slower, store plain values (`Vector3`, numbers, strings) in a table and draw only from that table.

- Avoid `FindFirstChild`, `GetChildren`, `.Character` or `.Position` reads inside `onPaint`, and avoid one loop per player.

If a frame lands while a script loop holds the VM, the last finished frame is shown again, so drawings do not flicker. Callbacks that stay too slow are removed; the limits are under Lua VM > Settings > Safety Limits.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **draw.Text(text, x, y, color?, font?, alpha?, scale?)** | `string, number, number, Color3?, string?, number?, number?` | Draws text at the top-left. Unknown font names fall back to the default font; `scale` multiplies the font size and skips drawing at 0 or below. |
| **draw.TextOutlined(text, x, y, color?, font?, alpha?, scale?)** | same | Draws text with a one-pixel black outline on four sides. |
| **draw.GetTextSize(text, font?, scale?)** | `string, string?, number?` | Returns `width, height`. Returns `0, 0` for a non-positive scale. |
| **draw.Line(x1, y1, x2, y2, color?, thickness?, alpha?)** | `number x4, Color3?, number?, number?` | Straight line. |
| **draw.Rect(x, y, w, h, color?, thickness?, rounding?, alpha?)** | `number x4, Color3?, number?, number?, number?` | Rectangle outline. |
| **draw.RectFilled(x, y, w, h, color?, rounding?, alpha?)** | `number x4, Color3?, number?, number?` | Filled rectangle. |
| **draw.Circle(cx, cy, radius, color?, thickness?, segments?, alpha?)** | `number x3, Color3?, number?, int?, number?` | Circle outline. Default segments: 12. |
| **draw.CircleFilled(cx, cy, radius, color?, segments?, alpha?)** | `number x3, Color3?, int?, number?` | Filled circle. Default segments: 12. |
| **draw.Triangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, color?, thickness?, alpha?)** | `number x6, Color3?, number?, number?` | Triangle outline. |
| **draw.TriangleFilled(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, color?, alpha?)** | `number x6, Color3?, number?` | Filled triangle. |
| **draw.Gradient(x, y, w, h, startColor?, endColor?, isHorizontal?, startAlpha?, endAlpha?)** | `number x4, Color3?, Color3?, bool?, number?, number?` | Two-color rectangle. Defaults: white to black, vertical. |
| **draw.Image(textureId, x, y, w, h, r, g, b, a)** | `int, number x4, int x4` | Draws an ImGui texture. Color and alpha are 0-255 integers. |
| **draw.Polyline(points, color?, closed?, thickness?, alpha?)** | `table, Color3?, bool?, number?, number?` | Connects `{ {x, y}, ... }` points. Needs at least two points. |
| **draw.ConvexPolyFilled(points, color?, alpha?)** | `table, Color3?, number?` | Fills a convex point list. Needs at least three points. |
| **draw.ComputeConvexHull(points)** | `table` | Returns the convex hull of a point list, as `{ {x, y}, ... }`. |
| **draw.GetPartCorners(part)** | `Instance` | Returns the eight world-space corners of a part as `Vector3` values, or `nil` for an invalid instance. |
| **draw.DeltaTime()** |  | Frame delta in seconds. |

### Example

```lua
local function onPaint()
    draw.Text("Hello World", 100, 100, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
    draw.RectFilled(50, 50, 200, 100, Color3.new(1, 0, 0), 4, 0.8)

    local w, h = draw.GetTextSize("Hello World", nil, 1.2)
    draw.Rect(98, 98, w + 4, h + 4, Color3.new(0, 0, 0), 1, 0, 0.8)
end

cheat.Register("onPaint", onPaint)
```

---

## gui

Creates scripted tabs in the Sheldon overlay. Draw their contents with imgui or draw.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **gui.AddTab(tabName, callback, showPreview?)** | `string, function, bool?` | Adds or replaces a runtime tab. The callback runs every frame while the tab is rendered. `showPreview` keeps the tab visible when the menu preview is active. |
| **gui.RemoveTab(tabName)** | `string` | Removes a runtime tab and releases the callback. |
| **gui.IsTab(tabName)** | `string` | Returns whether a tab with that name exists. |
| **gui.GetMenuState(checkForeground?)** | `bool?` | Returns whether the menu is open. With `true`, also requires Roblox to be the foreground window. |
| **gui.IsForeground()** |  | Returns whether Roblox is the foreground window. |
| **gui.GetWindowSize()** |  | Returns the overlay size as a `Vector2`. |

The tab callback runs on the render thread and must not yield. Do not call `task.wait` inside it. Start work in `task.spawn`, keep state in a Lua table, and render from the callback. The callback also shares the VM lock with every other script, so it is skipped for that frame if the lock is busy for more than 8 ms.

### Example

```lua
local enabled = false
local value = 0

gui.AddTab("My Script", function()
    imgui.SetNextWindowSize(320, 180, 0)
    imgui.Begin("My Script", 0)

    local changed
    changed, enabled = imgui.Checkbox("Enabled", enabled)
    changed, value = imgui.Slider("Value", value, 0, 100)

    imgui.Text("Value: " .. value)
    imgui.End()
end)
```

---

| **imgui.Button(text, w?, h?)** | `string, number?, number?` | `true` on click |
| **imgui.TabButton(text, w?, h?, active?)** | `string, number?, number?, bool?` | `true` on click |
| **imgui.Checkbox(text, v)** | `string, bool` | `changed, value` |
| **imgui.TickBox(text, v)** | `string, bool` | Themed tick box. Returns `changed, value` |
| **imgui.Slider(title, v, min, max)** | `string, number, number, number` | `changed, value` |
| **imgui.SliderInt(title, v, min, max)** | `string, int, int, int` | `changed, value` |
| **imgui.DragFloat(title, v, speed?, min?, max?, format?, disabled?)** | `string, number, number?, number?, number?, string?, bool?` | `changed, value`. Default format `"%.3f"` |
| **imgui.DragInt(title, v, speed?, min?, max?, format?, disabled?)** | `string, int, number?, int?, int?, string?, bool?` | `changed, value`. Default format `"%d"` |
| **imgui.DragFloat2(title, x, y, speed?, min?, max?, format?, disabled?)** | `string, number x2, ...` | Labeled row, returns `changed, x, y` |
| **imgui.DragFloat3(title, x, y, z, speed?, min?, max?, format?, disabled?)** | `string, number x3, ...` | Labeled row, returns `changed, x, y, z` |
| **imgui.InputText(title, v, placeholder, w?, flags?)** | `string, string, string, number?, int?` | `changed, value` |
| **imgui.MultilineInput(title, v, placeholder, w?, flags?)** | `string, string, string, number?, int?` | `changed, value` |
| **imgui.WidgetsText(text, color?, alpha?)** | `string, Color3?, number?` | Themed label with optional color. No return. |
| **imgui.BeginContent(title, h?, w?)** | `string, number?, number?` | Starts a themed content box. Returns whether it is visible / open. |
| **imgui.EndContent()** |  | Closes the box |
| **imgui.ColorPicker(title, color?, alpha?)** | `string, Color3?, number?` | `changed, Color3` |
| **imgui.ProgressBar(title, value01, width, divisions, align?)** | `string, number, number, int, string?` | `align` is `"Left"`, `"Center"` or `"Right"`. No return. |
| **imgui.Note(text)** | `string` | Small themed note. No return. |
| **imgui.ListBox(label, items, height?, w?, listHeight?)** | `string, table, int?, number?, number?` | `changed, selected`. `items` is a 1-based array of strings. |
| **imgui.Dropdown(title, items, current?)** | `string, table, string?` | `changed, current` |
| **imgui.Shimmer(w, h)** | `number, number` | Loading placeholder. No return. |

### Drag Widgets

`DragFloat` / `DragInt` are draggable numeric fields. Drag horizontally to change the value; click without dragging to type a value directly. Hold `Ctrl` while dragging for finer steps (0.1×), `Shift` for coarser (10×).

- `speed` – value change per pixel dragged (default `1`).

- `min`, `max` – clamp range. Leave both `0` (or equal) for an **unbounded** field.

- `format` – printf-style, may include a suffix, e.g. `"%.2f studs"` or `"%d rounds"`.

- `disabled` – when `true`, the field is dimmed and ignores input.

- `DragFloat2` / `DragFloat3` render a labeled property row with 2 / 3 boxes sharing one row's width – ideal for Vector2 / Vector3.

### Tabs

| Function | Signature | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **imgui.BeginTabs(title, enableAnim?)** | `string, bool?` | Returns whether the tab bar is visible |
| **imgui.BeginTab(name)** | `string` | Returns whether this tab is selected |
| **imgui.EndTab()** |  | Closes the current tab |
| **imgui.EndTabs()** |  | Closes the tab bar |

### Item State

| Function | Returns / notes |
| --- | --- |
| **imgui.IsItemHovered(flags?)** | `bool`. Optional ImGui hover flags |
| **imgui.IsItemActive()** | `bool` |
| **imgui.IsItemFocused()** | `bool` |
| **imgui.IsItemClicked(btn?)** | `bool`. Button defaults to 0 (left) |
| **imgui.IsAnyItemHovered()** | `bool` |
| **imgui.IsAnyItemActive()** | `bool` |
| **imgui.IsAnyItemFocused()** | `bool` |
| **imgui.GetItemRectMin()** | Returns `x, y` |
| **imgui.GetItemRectMax()** | Returns `x, y` |
| **imgui.GetItemRectSize()** | Returns `w, h` |
| **imgui.IsWindowHovered(flags?)** | `bool` |
| **imgui.IsWindowFocused(flags?)** | `bool` |

### Columns

| Function | Signature | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **imgui.Columns(count?, id?, border?)** | `int?, string?, bool?` | Defaults: 1 column, no id, border on |
| **imgui.NextColumn()** |  | Advances to the next column |
| **imgui.GetColumnIndex()** |  | Returns the current column index |
| **imgui.GetColumnWidth(index?)** | `int?` | Defaults to the current column |
| **imgui.SetColumnWidth(index, width)** | `int, number` | Sets a column's width |

### Example

```lua
imgui.Begin("My Window", 0)
imgui.Text("Hello, world!")
if imgui.Button("Click Me") then
    print("Button clicked!")
end

-- Drag widgets return (changed, newValue). Reassign to persist.
local changed, speed = imgui.DragFloat("Speed", speed, 0.5, 0, 100, "%.1f")
if changed then print("Speed is now", speed) end

-- Vector3 as a labeled 3-box row
local moved, px, py, pz = imgui.DragFloat3("Position", px, py, pz, 0.25)

-- A disabled (read-only looking) field
imgui.DragFloat("Locked", 42, 1, 0, 0, "%.2f", true)
imgui.End()
```

---

## fflags

FastFlag (FFlag) reading and writing utilities.

| Function | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **fflags.Get(name, type, original?)** | `string, string, bool?` | Reads a flag as `type`. `original` reads the startup value instead of the current value. Returns `nil` for an unknown flag or unsupported read type. |
| **fflags.Set(name, value)** | `string, any` | Writes a flag, choosing the width from the value. Returns `true`, or `nil` if the flag does not exist. |
| **fflags.Set(name, value, type)** | `string, any, string` | Writes a flag with an explicit type. Returns `true`, or `nil` for an unknown flag or unsupported write type. |
| **fflags.GetAll()** |  | Returns an array of `{ name, runtime, original }` entries for every loaded flag. |

### Types

`float`, `double`, `int`, `uint`, `bool`, `byte`, `short`, `ushort`, `int64`, `uint64`, `string`. Set also supports `pointer`.

When `Set` is called without a type, the width is decided from the value: integers in int32 range → `int32` (larger → `int64`), floats → `float`, booleans → `bool`, strings → `string`.

Flag names are read from the client's FFlag name cache and autocomplete from the first string argument. The type argument autocompletes the read or write types.

### Example

```lua
local val = fflags.Get("FFlagEnableVR", "bool")
print("VR enabled:", val)
fflags.Set("FFlagEnableVR", true)
fflags.Set("FFlagEnableVR", true, "bool")
```

---

## Instance

The wrapper around a live Roblox instance. Access instances through game, services, properties and child lookups.

### Properties

| Property | Type | Access | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Name** | `string` | RW | Instance name. Cannot be set on the DataModel. |
| **ClassName** | `string` | RO | Class name |
| **Parent** | `Instance` | RO | Parent instance. Re-parenting is not exposed. |
| **Address** | `uintptr` | RO | Raw memory address |
| **FullName** | `string` | RO | Full hierarchical path |

Every class property the VM can read is also available as a field. That includes the hand-written classes and everything in the game's reflection table. [Auto Complete](#/autocomplete) lists them per class. Read-only properties raise `'name' is read-only` when assigned.

### Methods

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **:FindFirstChild(name)** | `Instance\|nil` | Finds a direct child by exact name |
| **:WaitForChild(name, timeout?)** | `Instance\|nil` | Polls for a child every 25 ms until it appears or the timeout in seconds expires. This blocks the calling thread; do not use it in a render callback. |
| **:FindFirstChildOfClass(className)** | `Instance\|nil` | Finds a direct child by class |
| **:FindDescendants(name)** | `table` | Returns every descendant with that name |
| **:FindDescendantsOfClass(className)** | `table` | Returns every descendant of that class |
| **:GetChildren()** | `table` | Direct children |
| **:GetDescendants()** | `table` | All descendants |
| **:Ancestors()** | `table` | All ancestors |
| **:IsDescendantOf(ancestor)** | `bool` | Whether this instance is below `ancestor` |
| **:IsA(className)** | `bool` | Exact `ClassName` comparison. Unlike Roblox's `IsA`, base classes do not match. |
| **:IsAncestorOf(descendant)** | `bool` | Whether this instance is above `descendant` |
| **:GetAttributes()** | `table` | Returns a table with attribute names as keys and a matching array of names |
| **:GetAttribute(name)** | `string\|nil` | Reads a string attribute. Non-string attributes return `nil`. |
| **:SetAttribute(name, value)** |  | Writes an existing attribute. Supports `double`, `float`, `bool`, `int`, `Vector3` and `string` attributes. Unknown names and unsupported types are ignored. |
| **:GetTags()** | `table` | Array of collection tags |
| **:GetTag(tag)** | `string\|nil` | Returns the tag when present |
| **:HasTag(tag)** | `bool` | Checks for a tag |
| **:AddTag(tag)** | `bool` | Adds a tag |
| **:RemoveTag(tag)** | `bool` | Removes a tag |
| **:RenameTag(oldName, newName)** |  | Renames a tag |
| **:GetPropertyChangedSignal(property)** | `RBXScriptSignal` | Returns a signal that fires when the property changes |

### Signals

| Signal | Arguments | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Changed** | `propertyName, newValue` | Fires when a registered or reflected property changes |
| **ChildAdded** | `child` | Fires for new direct children |
| **DescendantAdded** | `descendant` | Fires for new descendants |
| **GetPropertyChangedSignal(property)** |  | Per-property signal, same connection API |

#### Example

```lua
local Workspace = game:GetService("Workspace")
local part = Workspace.Part

local sig = part:GetPropertyChangedSignal("Position")
sig:Connect(function()
    print("Position changed!")
end)

part.ChildAdded:Connect(function(child)
    print("new child:", child.Name, child.ClassName)
end)
```

`Changed`, `ChildAdded` and `DescendantAdded` are derived by polling the instance tree. They fire from the VM's scheduler, not from Roblox's own event system.

### Property lookup

- `instance.PropertyName` checks the built-in properties, then the three signals above, then the class property map, then the game's reflected property table, then direct children by name.

- Writing goes through the class property map and then reflected properties. Read-only fields raise an error. `ClassName`, `Parent`, `Address`, `FullName` and the built-in signals cannot be assigned.

- `for k, v in pairs(instance) do ... end` builds a snapshot table of built-ins, class properties, reflected properties and children.

### DataModel

The global `game` is the Roblox `DataModel`. There is no `Game` or `workspace` global; use `game:GetService("Workspace")`.

`DataModel` inherits from `Instance`, so all Instance methods are available.

#### GetService

| Method | Returns | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **:GetService(className)** | `Instance\|nil` | Get service by class name |

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")
```

---

## RemoteEvent

RemoteEvent, UnreliableRemoteEvent and RemoteFunction use the standard Instance API in this build.

**No extra Lua members:** this build does not add `FireServer`, `InvokeServer`, `OnFireServer`, `OnClientEvent` or the other remote-spy signals to remote instances. The engine has an internal remote spy, but it is not exposed to Lua yet.

Remote instances still support every [Instance](#/instance) property and method: `Name`, `ClassName`, `Parent`, `FullName`, children, attributes, tags and signals. Find them like any other object:

```lua
local remotes = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage"):FindFirstChild("Remotes")
local event = remotes and remotes:FindFirstChild("MyEvent")

if event then
    print(event.ClassName, event.Name, event.FullName)
end
```

---

## Custom Types

The five value types the VM binds: Vector3, Vector2, Color3, UDim and UDim2. They are not Roblox userdata and do not have the full Roblox API.

### Vector3

```lua
Vector3.new()           -- (0, 0, 0)
Vector3.new(x, y, z)
Vector3.new(n)          -- (n, n, n)
```

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| .x / .y / .z | float | Mutable components. `.X` / `.Y` / `.Z` are aliases. |
| .Magnitude | float | Read-only length |
| .Unit | Vector3 | Read-only normalized vector; zero stays zero |

**Operators:** `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` component-wise with another Vector3 or a Vector2 (the z component is kept), unary `-`, and `tostring`. Scalar multiplication and division are not bound.

### Vector2

```lua
Vector2.new()           -- (0, 0)
Vector2.new(x, y)
Vector2.new(n)          -- (n, n)
```

| Member | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| .x / .y | float | Mutable components. `.X` / `.Y` are aliases. |
| **:Magnitude()** | float | Method, not a property. Call `v:Magnitude()`. |
| .Unit | Vector2 | Read-only normalized vector |

**Operators:** `+`, `-`, `*`, `/` with another Vector2 or Vector3 (the result is a Vector3), unary `-`, and `tostring`.

### Color3

```lua
Color3.new(r, g, b)     -- if any component is > 1, all are divided by 255
Color3.fromRGB(r, g, b) -- 0-255 integers
Color3.fromHSV(h, s, v) -- h is 0-360 degrees
Color3.fromHex("#ff8800")
```

| Member | Type |
| --- | --- |
| .r | float |
| .g | float |
| .b | float |

**Static values are functions:** `Color3.White()`, `Color3.Red()`, `Color3.Green()`, `Color3.Blue()`, `Color3.Yellow()`, `Color3.Black()`. Calling them without parentheses returns a function, not a color.

### UDim

```lua
local u = UDim.new()   -- UDim(0, 0)
u.Scale = 0.5
u.Offset = 10
```

| Property | Type | Access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| .Scale | float | RW |
| .Offset | int | RW |

`UDim.new` only accepts zero arguments. Use a `UDim2`'s `X` / `Y` fields, or create an empty UDim and assign the fields. Operators: `+`, `-`, `tostring`.

### UDim2

```lua
UDim2.new()                                          -- 0,0, 0,0
UDim2.new(UDim x, UDim y)
UDim2.new(float xs, int xo, float ys, int yo)
UDim2.fromScale(float xs, float ys)
UDim2.fromOffset(int xo, int yo)
UDim2.Lerp(UDim2 a, UDim2 b, float alpha)
```

| Property | Type | Access |
| --- | --- | --- |
| .X | UDim | RW |
| .Y | UDim | RW |

Operators: `+`, `-`, `tostring`. `UDim2.Lerp` is a static function on the type table, not a method on a value.

#### Example

```lua
local u = UDim2.fromOffset(100, 50)
local v = UDim2.new(0.5, 0, 0, 20)
local result = u + v

local udim = UDim.new()
udim.Scale = 0.5
udim.Offset = 10
print(udim.Scale, udim.Offset)

print(Color3.Red())
```

---

## RBXScriptSignal (Events)

Roblox-style connections backed by the VM scheduler.

```lua
local connection = signal:Connect(function(...)
    print(...)
end)

connection:Disconnect()  -- removes only this callback
connection:Stop()        -- stops the script slot that owns the callback

-- Inside a coroutine: yields until the next fire and returns its arguments.
task.spawn(function()
    local a, b = signal:Wait()
end)
```

`Connect` returns a connection table. `Wait` raises `Cannot call Wait on the main thread - use task.spawn` when called from the script body, because it needs a coroutine to suspend.

Callbacks run on the VM worker thread. They can yield. An error inside a callback is caught and does not disconnect the other callbacks.

### Built-in Signals

| Signal | Arguments | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Players.PlayerAdded** | `Player` | Fires when a new player is detected |
| **Players.PlayerRemoving** | `Player` | Fires when a player leaves |
| **Player.CharacterAdded** | `Model` | Fires when the player's character spawns |
| **Player.CharacterRemoving** | `Model` | Fires before the character is removed |
| **Player.CharacterAppearanceLoaded** | `Model` | Fires after the character's appearance loads |
| **Instance.Changed** | `propertyName, newValue` | Fires when a registered or reflected property changes |
| **Instance.ChildAdded** | `child` | Fires for new direct children |
| **Instance.DescendantAdded** | `descendant` | Fires for new descendants |
| **Instance:GetPropertyChangedSignal(name)** |  | Per-property signal with the same connection API |

`PlayerAdded`, `PlayerRemoving` and the character signals are registered on the `Player` / `Players` classes. Instance signals and property signals are derived by polling the instance tree from the scheduler, so they can arrive a scheduler tick late.

### Example

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    print("joined:", player.Name, player.UserId)
end)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
    print("left:", player.Name)
end)

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
if player then
    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
        print("spawned:", character.Name)
    end)
end
```

---

## Library Gating

Five libraries are switched off by default and throw until enabled in the Lua VM settings.

| Library | Gated functions | Error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Memory** | All `memory.*` | `'Memory' library is not enabled` |
| **Clipboard** | `utility.GetClipboard`, `utility.SetClipboard` | `Clipboard library is not enabled` |
| **File_Management** | All `file.*` | `'File_Management' library is not enabled` |
| **Input** | All `input.*` | `'Input' library is not enabled` |
| **Internet** | All `internet.*` | `'Internet' library is not enabled` |

Open the Lua VM's Settings popup and enable the toggle under **Libraries**. The change applies to the running VM immediately; scripts do not need to be restarted. Toggles are not persisted across a full Sheldon restart in this build.

[Auto Complete](#/autocomplete) marks a disabled library's members as `[Disabled]` and inserts the name without making it callable.

---

## Notes

Additional implementation details and behavior notes.

- The VM runs Lua 5.4, not Luau. Only `base`, `math`, `table` and `string` are opened. There is no `coroutine`, `os`, `io`, `utf8`, `bit32` or `debug` library exposed to scripts.

- Luau type ascriptions (`local x: Type`, `value :: Type`) are removed before compilation. Compound assignments `+=`, `-=`, `*=`, `/=`, `%=`, `**=`, `..=`, `&=`, `|=`, `>=` are expanded. `continue`, generalized iteration and Luau-only syntax are not supported.

- `pcall` and `xpcall` are replaced so a stopped script can interrupt protected calls. The VM also checks its stop flag from a Lua instruction hook every 10 instructions.

- Scripts run on a worker thread. `task.wait` and `RBXScriptSignal:Wait` need a coroutine and raise on the main script body. `WaitForChild` blocks the calling thread instead of yielding.

- `print()` writes with a `[print]` prefix and `warn()` with `[warn]`. Runtime errors go to the console as `[error]`.

- `tick()` returns `GetTickCount64()`, milliseconds since system start, not UNIX time.

- `loadstring` also strips type ascriptions. It returns `(function, nil)` or `(nil, error_message)`.

- Instance reads check built-ins, signals, the class property map, the game's reflected properties, then direct children. Writes go through the class map and reflected properties. Read-only writes raise an error; they do not fail silently.

- `Instance:IsA` compares the exact `ClassName`; base classes do not match. `Parent` is read-only in this build.

- `game` is the only DataModel global. There is no `Game` or `workspace` global; use `game:GetService("Workspace")`.

- `string.regex` uses C++ `std::regex` with ECMAScript syntax, so it expects `\d+`, not Lua's `%d+`.

- File, HTTP response, HTTP request-body, base64, hash and compress inputs are capped at 10 MB. File listings stop at 256 entries.

- HTTP requires `https://` unless Require HTTPS is turned off in the Lua VM settings. Timeouts are 1-15000 ms, default 5000.

- `compress.Compress` does not store the original size, but `compress.Decompress` expects a 4-byte header. The two functions do not round-trip in this build.

- Remote spy members and `FireServer` / `InvokeServer` are not exposed to Lua. Remote instances use the standard Instance API.

- The old Class Properties page is deprecated. The live property list comes from [Auto Complete](#/autocomplete) and the game's reflection table.
